finding: None of the sites, vendors or papers found forecasts occupancy per cell class 1–14 days ahead. Plants with similar AWs keep design headroom or expand (Cadel keeps about 33% expansion reserve, Growermetal reports running at 50% saturation, Rubbermaid saw floor staging). The closest commercial idea is a Dynamics 365 add-on that forecasts pallet space per week from planned transactions.
implication_for_coster: The tool is new, not a copy of an existing product. The plan-driven flow balance is the same idea as the closest commercial feature, which supports rung 2.
action: Say this in the canvases (value proposition, no off-the-shelf alternative). Keep the Dynamics add-on and the Odoo 'full in X days' alert as the comparison points.
confidence: medium (absence of evidence after a broad search; web search was rate-limited)

finding: Keeping tall or wide cells free for loads that need them is a documented WMS rule (VI-MA, Mecalux: taller locations reserved for taller pallets across three heights).
implication_for_coster: The 110 wide cells that stayed free on 20 May are most likely such a reservation, not random behaviour.
action: Model it as a reservation parameter per class in the allocation cascade, fit it on the 20 May snapshot, and ask Coster or the WMS vendor for the real parameter.

finding: A WMS named WLog is made by Wise Ingegneria e Soluzioni Software (Brusaporto, Bergamo). Its pages describe loading algorithms based on the physical structure of the material, ABC and configurable criteria, an unattended nightly reorganisation, and floor areas up to the factory boundary. No public source names Coster as a customer.
implication_for_coster: If Coster's WLog is this product, the allocation rules, the defrag (reorganisation) trigger and the floor-buffer locations are all configurable WMS features with documented parameters.
action: Ask Coster to confirm the vendor. Then ask for the allocation and reorganisation parameters and the table documentation (cells, missions, floor locations).
confidence: medium (vendor match likely, Coster link unconfirmed)

finding: An Econerre article (2020, hosted by E80) says Elettric80 and BEMA developed the first smart-factory model in Caldonazzo di Trento for Costerplast in 1992, and that the technology was later used in the other Coster Group plants. E80 sells LGV systems with WMS-level software and a simulation tool (SmartDesigner).
implication_for_coster: Coster's LGV system may come from E80. The LGV mission database could then be a ready source of actual flows.
action: Ask Coster who supplies the LGVs and whether the LGV mission log can be exported.
confidence: medium (the 1992 Costerplast link is stated by the source, that today's LGVs come from E80 is not)

finding: Reorganisation or compaction in idle time is a named function in AS/RS software (Automha, Mecalux slotting moves only above a benefit threshold, Moffett rearranges in quiet periods). Papers treat reshuffling as a time-limited problem in idle periods. A 2025 plant study found smaller real gains because next-day plans were incomplete.
implication_for_coster: Defrag frees cells in the critical classes without any flow in or out, limited by idle crane time.
action: Model defrag as a capacity-recovery flow with a threshold and an idle-time budget. Use Coster's defrag rules when they arrive.

finding: Unit-load literature defines a rack service level as the probability that all pallets present can be stored, per slot height (Cardona & Gue). Rigid storage classes need more space than average inventory suggests (Guo, Yu & de Koster).
implication_for_coster: This explains why 84% total fill hid a full Medium class, and it gives a formal KPI for 'pallets with no compatible free cell'.
action: Report a per-class service level next to the fill ratio. Add a small max-flow feasibility check over load-unit types × cell classes to separate policy-caused overflow from real lack of space.

finding: The data most often used by comparable models, and missing from Coster's current request, is: floor-buffer occupancy and floor↔AW transfers, daily cell status, a load-unit ID shared across SAP/WLog/LGV/MES, the meaning of each timestamp (event vs record time), a layout and rule change log, the factory calendar, production confirmations and plan-vs-actual dates, supplier confirmations/ASNs with goods-receipt times, and the customer order book.
implication_for_coster: Without these, part of the flow stays invisible (the plan gap) and the backtest cannot be honest.
action: Add the items marked coster_file_ref = new (view v_data_missing_from_request) to the next data request, must-haves first.

finding: Evaluating forecasts on final (revised) data overstates accuracy and can change which method looks best (data vintages, leakage, forecast-evaluation pitfalls). In SAP, change documents (CDHDR/CDPOS) and scheduled vs actual order dates (AFKO) can partly rebuild past plans.
implication_for_coster: Coster keeps no plan history, so every backtest before the archive starts uses an optimistic plan.
action: Archive the plan exports every day from now on. Ask whether SAP change documents are active for purchase and production orders.

finding: WMS and ERP stock records are often wrong (an empirical study found about 65% of inventory records inaccurate). A validated AS/RS simulation method reached a 0.49% median error against the real system, after calibrating the model on measured data.
implication_for_coster: The 06:00 snapshot is the best available state but not ground truth. A simulator can be accurate if it is calibrated on real data and checked with a mass balance.
action: Run the mass-balance (Little's law) check per class before forecasting. Calibrate the simulator's timing and rule parameters on Coster's real data and get the real allocation rules.

finding: Hospital census forecasting solves the same problem: occupancy = today's patients × the chance each is still there + scheduled admissions × length-of-stay survival, with Poisson-binomial sums or Monte Carlo for the band. Expert discharge dates are blended with LOS statistics (Bos 2025). Baas 2021 put 3-day maximum-occupancy forecasts into hospital dashboards.
implication_for_coster: Each occupied cell is a 'patient' with a planned exit (ship date or consumption) plus an empirical deviation. This gives P(>80%) and P(>90%) per class directly.
action: Build rung 2's outflow side this way. Ask for the goods-receipt date per load unit in the snapshot and stable load-unit IDs. Dwell times from before August may still be usable, because they depend on the material, not the layout.

finding: Shipment notices behave like bookings. In car parks, airlines and hotels, the additive advanced pickup method (bookings on hand + expected bookings still to come) beat multiplicative and pure time-series methods, with short training windows.
implication_for_coster: Outbound beyond the 24–72 h notice horizon (days 3–14) can be forecast from the notice curve instead of guessed.
action: Log notices with their arrival time from now on, and fit an additive pickup model for outbound pallets per day.

finding: On fev-bench, covariate support decides the foundation-model ranking: Chronos-2 leads (91.4% probabilistic win rate), then TiRex and TimesFM-2.5. Only some models take known-future covariates (Chronos-2, TabPFN-TS, TimesFM via XReg). With under about 700 samples, zero-shot beats fine-tuning. TimesFM 3.0 and Moirai 2.0 weights are non-commercial.
implication_for_coster: Chronos-2 (Apache-2.0, runs on CPU for 5 series) is the right rung 4 candidate, used zero-shot with plans as covariates. TabPFN-TS in local mode is the second opinion.
action: Wire Chronos-2 now on the fev-bench covariate tasks, then on Coster's data. Do not fine-tune on the short history.

finding: In M5, the top methods trained one global model across many series and all used external information. With very short history, regularised linear models are the safer first step.
implication_for_coster: Rung 3 should be one model per horizon, trained on all 5 classes together, correcting the simulator's residuals.
action: Start with Ridge on plan and calendar features (about 70 days of data), move to a small LightGBM when history grows.

finding: Per-horizon split conformal gave valid 90% intervals with narrow width in a 2026 benchmark. ACI adapts after shifts. The probability of crossing 90% within 48 h needs joint sample paths, not per-day intervals. Alerts are scored with the Brier score and CORP reliability diagrams. Poisson arrivals and fixed parameters make bands too narrow.
implication_for_coster: The uncertainty layer can stay simple, but the threshold probability must come from simulated paths with correlated plan slips.
action: Wrap each rung with per-horizon split conformal + ACI. Compute p_critical_by from Monte Carlo or bootstrapped paths. Report coverage per horizon.

finding: At Infineon, a simulation started every night from the current fab state forecast WIP 7 days ahead, and showed traffic lights next to the last 3 days of forecast vs actual, which built trust. Starting a simulation from a wrong initial state gives wrong results (Gunn & Nahavandi).
implication_for_coster: The daily run from the 06:00 snapshot is a proven pattern. Showing recent forecast vs actual helps adoption.
action: Add a 'last 3 days: forecast vs actual' strip per class to the dashboard (Group 2).

finding: Regime changes break both models and intervals. Change-point detection dates the break. Capacity-forecasting practice argues an alert system should be able to say 'I don't know' after such a change.
implication_for_coster: The August layout change and any later rule change must cut the training window, and alerts should abstain when data is too short.
action: Run ruptures (PELT) on the occupancy history to date the break. Add an 'insufficient data' state to the alert logic.

finding: No public dataset combines cell-class occupancy, plans and flows. Useful stand-ins: an Italian-WMS-like movement log (VillanovaAI), warehouse dwell-time tables (Carreras; Lineage records on request), hotel bookings for the plan-plus-stay chain, fev-bench covariate tasks for Chronos-2, and parking or NHS bed data for short-history baselines.
implication_for_coster: The whole pipeline can be built and tested before Coster's files arrive.
action: Use VillanovaAI for the parser and schemas, Hotel Booking for the end-to-end chain, fev-bench for rung 4. Email the Lineage authors for their dwell-time data now.
